correctness.rationale:
The direct-product identities reconstruct from definitions: the adjoint of a symplectic direct sum is the direct sum of adjoints, the integral subgroup is the direct sum of integral subgroups, and finite indices therefore multiply. Iteration gives \(
u(\Lambda^{\oplus k})=
u^k\) and \(
u((\Lambda^{\oplus k})^\circ)=r^k\). Substitution into the cited exact multiwindow classification gives \(q_{\min}^{\mathcal S}=\lceil(r^k+kd)/
u^kceil\), hence the one-window condition \(
u^k-r^k\ge kd\). For \((d,
u,r)=(2,2,1)\), the values are exactly \(2,2,1\) for the first three powers. The asymptotic activation follows because the positive exponential lower bound dominates \(kd\).
